title: The category of modules over a ring is Grothendieck abelian
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $\Mod(R)$ the category of (left) $R$-modules and $R$-linear maps, an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Then $\Mod(R)$ is a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]: it has all small colimits, filtered colimits in $\Mod(R)$ are exact (a filtered colimit of short exact sequences of $R$-modules is a short exact sequence), and it has a generator, namely the $R$-module $R$ (for $R$-modules $N\subsetneq M$, a map $R\to M$, $1\mapsto m$ with $m\in M\setminus N$, does not factor through $N$).
